name: Fossar de la Pedrera, Montjuïc
story: This old quarry in Montjuïc cemetery was used as a common grave for people executed by the Franco regime after Barcelona fell on 26 January 1939, most of them shot at the Camp de la Bóta. Victims of the air raids and the city's poorest were also buried here. Lluís Companys, President of the Generalitat, was handed over by the Gestapo in occupied France, tried by court-martial and shot at Montjuïc castle on 15 October 1940; he lies in the mausoleum here. The site was made into a memorial in 1985, with columns listing the names of the executed. Nearby there are also memorials to the CNT dead, to the International Brigades and to Catalans who died in Nazi camps.
see: A quiet sunken garden in the old quarry, with stone columns listing the victims' names, the Companys mausoleum, the 'Pietat' sculpture and several other memorials along the paths.
plan: Inside Montjuïc cemetery (free, open daily); bus 21 to the cemetery gate, then follow the signs; allow time to walk the sloping paths.

boxes.text: Figures differ: about 1,717 executions in Barcelona are documented for 1939–52 (plaques give 1,734 for Camp de la Bóta), while some sources give around 4,000 burials in the grave, including bombing victims.
